correctness.rationale: For iid Bernoulli(p) input with 0<p<1, the past and future output half-lines separated by one unobserved index share exactly one input bit. Conditional independence and a rank-one covariance identity reduce their independence to one boundary-shielding condition. Four pair states and the invariant reachable spans prove that output words of length at most three suffice for an all-length certificate. Exact 256-rule symbolic gcd enumeration gives 32 all-bias rules and 24 extra rules at p=1/2, with no other interior roots; exact second-lag conditional expectations give seven pairwise-exception biases. The Rule-22 block witness has exact gap 32/6561. The standalone checker was executed on the actual package and separately checks rational biases via direct nine-bit enumeration. No experiment is promoted into an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Finite-dependence of local Bernoulli factors is a natural invariant, while pairwise correlations can misdiagnose joint independence. The exact count changes only at the fair input bias even though the two-point test has seven explicit algebraic resonances, including golden-ratio and square-root biases. The Rule-22 rational covariance witness gives a concrete intrinsic counterexample to pairwise-test sufficiency, and the full 256-rule classification is a natural complete family rather than an arbitrary slice. The structural four-state shielding lemma is reusable for other finite-range factors.
